declarations.en: Let $N$ be a natural number and let the supplied model $M$ consist of an intermediate field $F$ between $ℚ$ and the fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field $ℚ(t)$ in an indeterminate $t$, with elements $u,v∈F$. Assume that no nonzero polynomial over $ℚ$ vanishes at $u$, that $u^N+v^N=1$, that the subfield generated by $ℚ,u,v$ is all of $F$, and that $F$ is finite dimensional over the subfield $ℚ(u)$ with dimension exactly $N$. For $N=0$ the equation would be $1+1=1$ in characteristic zero, so there is no such model and an assertion conditional on it is vacuous. A place $P$ means a proper valuation subring $O_P⊊F$ containing every rational number. Its residue field is $κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P$, where $𝔪_P$ is the maximal ideal of $O_P$. All such places are included; no affine chart is selected. Assume $h_{DVR}$: every $O_P$ is a discrete valuation ring. Let $v_P(f)$ be its normalized integer order, defined as minus the integer logarithm of the maximal-ideal valuation at $f$; the total-function convention is $v_P(0)=0$. A divisor is a finitely supported integer-valued function on all these places; equality of divisors means equality of every coefficient. For $f∈F$ write $b_f(P)=\max(0,-v_P(f))$ for its pole multiplicity and $B_f$ for the finite-support divisor with these coefficients. In particular $B_0=0$ under the stated convention. This defines the divisor $D_∞$ whose coefficient at every place is $D_∞(P)=\max(b_u(P),b_v(P))=\max(\max(0,-v_P(u)),\max(0,-v_P(v)))$, with finite support supplied by the construction. No positivity hypothesis on $N$ is a separate parameter of this definition, and its coefficients range over all places, including places where a coordinate has a pole.

declarations.en: Let $N$ be a natural number and let the supplied model $M$ consist of an intermediate field $F$ between $ℚ$ and the fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field $ℚ(t)$ in an indeterminate $t$, with elements $u,v∈F$. Assume that no nonzero polynomial over $ℚ$ vanishes at $u$, that $u^N+v^N=1$, that the subfield generated by $ℚ,u,v$ is all of $F$, and that $F$ is finite dimensional over the subfield $ℚ(u)$ with dimension exactly $N$. For $N=0$ the equation would be $1+1=1$ in characteristic zero, so there is no such model and an assertion conditional on it is vacuous. A place $P$ means a proper valuation subring $O_P⊊F$ containing every rational number. Its residue field is $κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P$, where $𝔪_P$ is the maximal ideal of $O_P$. All such places are included; no affine chart is selected. Assume $h_{DVR}$: every $O_P$ is a discrete valuation ring. Let $v_P(f)$ be its normalized integer order, defined as minus the integer logarithm of the maximal-ideal valuation at $f$; the total-function convention is $v_P(0)=0$. A divisor is a finitely supported integer-valued function on all these places; equality of divisors means equality of every coefficient. For $f∈F$ write $b_f(P)=\max(0,-v_P(f))$ for its pole multiplicity and $B_f$ for the finite-support divisor with these coefficients. In particular $B_0=0$ under the stated convention. Assume additionally $h_{RF}$: $κ(P)$ is finite dimensional over $ℚ$ for every place $P$; this assumption is an explicit parameter of this declaration. The degree of a place is $d_P=\dim_{ℚ}κ(P)$, the finite rational vector-space dimension, and a divisor $A$ has integer degree $\deg A=\sum_P A(P)d_P$, summed over its finite support. For $f∈F$, define the integer $e_f(P)$ as follows: if $f∈O_P$, let $m_{P,f}∈ℚ[X]$ be the minimal polynomial over $ℚ$ of the residue $f+𝔪_P$ in the full residue field $κ(P)$ and put $e_f(P)=v_P(m_{P,f}(f))$; otherwise put $e_f(P)=-v_P(f)$. A supplied canonical-divisor datum, named $K$ in the signature, consists of a finite-support divisor $D_K$ with coefficient $D_K(P)=e_u(P)-1$ if $u∈O_P$ and $D_K(P)=-e_u(P)-1$ if $u∉O_P$, together with proofs of those equalities at every place. An infinity-divisor datum $H$ consists of a divisor $D_H$ and proofs of the exact equalities $D_H(P)=\max(b_u(P),b_v(P))$ for every place $P$; it is not merely a divisor of some prescribed degree. An adjunction datum $J$ for these particular $K,H$ consists of an actual element $r∈F$, a proof $r≠0$, and the coefficientwise identity $D_K(P)=(N-3)D_H(P)+v_P(r)$ for every place $P$. The subtraction $N-3$ is in the integers. No assumption says that every element of $F$ algebraic over $ℚ$ already belongs to $ℚ$. Assume $3<N$ and that these particular canonical, infinity and adjunction data are supplied. Then $\deg D_K=N(N-3)$, the integer named `planeCanonicalDegree N`. This is a conditional degree equality consuming the actual coefficient identity and its nonzero element $r$; it does not assert existence of $K$, $H$ or $J$. No identification with an independently defined differential is a separate conclusion of this signature.
